title: FIFA opts against action over Israeli teams playing in West Bank
content:
FIFA has opted not to take action against the Israel Football Association (IFA) regarding its teams playing in the West Bank after a complaint was lodged by the Palestinian Football Association (PFA) in 2024.

FIFA’s Governance, Audit and Compliance Committee (GACC) determined no action should be taken as “the final legal status of the West Bank remains an unresolved and highly complex matter under public international law”.

FIFA had opened two investigations into Israeli football, one in relation to teams from Israeli settlements in the West Bank competing in national Israeli competitions — a long-standing complaint of the PFA — and a second into allegations of discrimination by the IFA. FIFA is not taking action over the former, but the IFA has been sanctioned regarding the latter.

A statement released on FIFA’s website on Thursday stated that the GACC, one of FIFA’s four independent committees, had concluded that the governing body “should take no action given that, in the context of the interpretation of the relevant provisions of the FIFA Statutes, the final legal status of the West Bank remains an unresolved and highly complex matter under public international law”.

“FIFA should continue to promote dialogue and offer mediation between the Palestine Football Association and The Israel Football Association at an operational level,” the statement added.

“In this context, FIFA will continue to facilitate structured engagement and monitor developments.”

Israel has rejected claims from The United Nations (UN) and the International Court of Justice that all Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank area violate international law, according to the New York Times.

FairSquare, a non-profit organisation and advocacy group that focuses mainly on global labour migration rights, political repression and sport, has criticised the decision to take no action against Israeli teams playing in the West Bank.

“With today’s statement they (FIFA) have taken a dishonest approach in the face of unquestionably unlawful policies and practices on Israel’s part,” Nick McGeehan, a director at FairSquare, said in a statement to The Athletic.

“FIFA might well wish that the issue of Israeli settlements was a grey area in international law but UN Security Council Resolutions 446 and 2334, the decisions of the International Court of Justice in 2004 and 2024, and the consistent opinions of the world’s pre-eminent international lawyers prove otherwise. Its decision to dismiss the case can be added to the long list of instances of serial misgovernance.”

FIFA’s independent disciplinary committee has punished the IFA for failing to take action against racist and discriminatory behaviour.

In the same 2024 complaint, which was lodged at the FIFA Congress in Bangkok, the PFA accused the IFA of allowing Beitar Jerusalem, an Israeli Premier League side, to get away with racist and discriminatory behaviour.

The IFA was also accused of failing to act following social media posts showing support for the war in Gaza from the CEO of the Israeli Professional Football Leagues and from Israeli Premier League side FC Maccabi Netanya.

A document detailing the FIFA disciplinary committee’s investigation concluded: “In particular, by failing to condemn or remediate discriminatory practices and exclusionary policies— particularly those affecting Palestinians—the IFA has become institutionally complicit in a system that violates the core values of the game.”

Following the investigation, it was announced on Thursday that the IFA has been hit with multiple sanctions.

It has been fined CHF 150,000 ($289,000) and also ordered to display in its next three “A-level FIFA competition matches at home a significant and highly visible banner with the words ‘Football Unites the World – No to Discrimination’ alongside the Israel Football Association’s logo”.

The IFA must also implement a FIFA-approved “prevention plan” focused on “reforms, protocols, monitoring, and educational campaigns in stadiums and on official channels for an entire season”. The decision remains subject to any potential appeal.
